proposals.evidence: Ordered male + child components, comparing the contracted Tamil formation. Sri Lanka Educational Publications Department, Tamil11, printed p.112 (https://noolaham.net/project/795/79443/79443.pdf), visually verified, explicitly pairs āmpiḷai with āṇpiḷḷai in its colloquial/standard table. DEDR399 supplies āṇ male and4198 piḷḷai child. Survey contractions preserve these components; source vowel/rhotic variants remain unchanged, and borrowing versus shared formation across varieties is not resolved by this component analysis. See tamil-contracted-kinship-evidence.md.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3682 explicitly gives Tamil niṟaiya abundantly/plentifully, Malayalam niṟa fullness and Kannada neṟe fullness/completeness. These surveyed niraya/neriya-type many responses are comparative quantity uses of that documented fullness family. Minority lects absent from the article and possible local Tamil transmission remain subject to review; no literal attestation for those lects is claimed. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5159 gives Tamil/Malayalam āṟu river with Tamil oblique āṟṟu-. These survey ārɨ/āru/āttɨ river responses are comparative simple-stem correspondences, retaining the rhotic/geminate and final-vowel transcriptions. Minority lects absent from the article are not presented as literal attestations; inheritance versus local transmission remains reviewable. Longer river-bank and large-river responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
